newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX could reach 3,050 points in 1997 - DWS.
newsitem.headline: German DAX could reach 3,050 points in 1997 - DWS.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of shares could rise by 10 percent in coming months and a level of 3,050 points in 1997 is attainable, Deutsche Bank's German funds unit DWS said on Thursday.

"A DAX level of 3,050 points could be reached in 1997, based on ratios for 1997 of twenty times earnings and for 1998 of nearly 15 times earnings," said Christian Strenger, chairman of DWS fund managers.
The DAX-30 index of Germany's blue-chips ended bourse trade in Frankfurt at 2,772.34 points on Thursday.
The main investment themes for the coming year will include the continued low interest rate environment in most capital markets, including Germany, France and especially Japan, Strenger said.

The increasing globalisation of financial markets would continue to be of benefit to international companies, DWS said, while increased demands on management, particularly in the area of shareholder value, will also be a theme for investors next year.
